diagnosis.root_cause_boundary: The same DLRM request timed out through both the host NodePort and a direct Kubernetes port-forward while health and metrics remained responsive. After the port-forward timeout Triton reported one pending DLRM request and no second execution, localizing the observed stall to the Triton scheduler/model-instance path after the first successful DLRM inference. Whether tracing, the Triton PyTorch backend, or model-instance lifecycle causes the stall remains unproven.
diagnosis.windows_tcp_observation: The NodePort snapshot included CLOSE_WAIT, FIN_WAIT_2, and TIME_WAIT sockets, but the independent port-forward reproduced the timeout; these socket states are not accepted as the root cause.

next_action: Preserve this suite permanently as zero-credit. Run a bounded non-credit isolation diagnostic using the same immutable failed-suite artifact: repeated DLRM inference in the pinned Triton image outside Triton, Triton with frozen tracing enabled, and Triton with tracing disabled. Keep the frozen request payload and ten-second timeout; do not alter Q0, workload, thresholds, topology, batching, or matrix until the backend fault is evidenced.
